title: Star Rating Comparison Table
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Instructional Design; Data Presentation
description: Interactive HTML and CSS comparison table of five MicroSim libraries with color-coded star ratings, difficulty badges, row tooltips and two weight sliders that compute and sort a weighted score, so learners can judge which library best fits a stated need. Ratings are invented illustrations.

educational.audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners
educational.topic: Star rating comparison tables and weighted criteria
learningObjectives: The learner will judge which of several items best fits a stated need, by comparing star ratings, badges and tooltip descriptions across weighted criteria.

simulation.model: Weighted average of two ordinal ratings

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Evaluation against weighted criteria with justification
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Weight, sort, inspect tooltips and badges, judge
keyQuestions: Which criterion matters more for this stated need, and by how much?
Would you still choose the top-ranked item after reading its badge and description?
commonMisconceptions: The highest star total is always the best choice, regardless of the need.
A weighted score is objective, although the weights are a judgment.
assessmentOpportunities: Choose weights for a new need and justify the selected library
Explain a limitation of star ratings
